newsitem.title: USA: OPTIONS - Dollar vols firm, off post-Tankan peaks.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - Dollar vols firm, off post-Tankan peaks.

text.p: Implied volatilities for short-dated forex options were firmer Wednesday but off peaks hit overnight as traders digested the Bank of Japan's surprising quarterly business sentiment survey, brokers said.
The Tankan index showed unexpected optimism among big manufacturers and initially shoved dollar/yen toward 113.30 on ideas that Japan's economy might withstand a rate hike.

But at second glance the report revealed divergent moods between major manufacturers and other companies, which stifled the rate-hike speculation and helped spot dollar/yen claw back up toward 114.00.

"Certainly that's (Tankan) why the front-end vols in dollar/yen are quite a bit higher," a bank options trader said. "Yen vols are up about a vol in the front end and maybe a little bit less in the back end. But with the (dollar) move down overnight, it's better bid. Clearly, people are leery about the downside here."
One-week yen was quoted at about 13.0/14.0 percent Wednesday morning, up from 11.0 percent Tuesday.
One-month yen hung at 11.3/11.6 percent, slightly below the morning's level and well off the high bid near 12.4 percent paid overnight. On Tuesday, it stood near 10.75/11.0.
"It's off from overnight activity but clearly still higher than yesterday by almost three-quarters of a vol," the trader said.
Yen 25 delta risk reversal tilted further in favor of yen calls, firming to 2.3/2.8 from 2.0/2.4 points Tuesday.
Among talked-about deals, a New York investment bank reportedly bought size in six-month yen calls in a 30-delta risk reversal trading at around 0.8 point.
Brokers said the bank bought one yard of the calls Tuesday and apparently bought another $200 million worth overnight. It was unclear whether the trades were customer or proprietary.
Also of interest was a very slight skew toward sterling puts, with that risk reversal quoted at about 0.1/0.25 points.

"They're buying sterling, but the sterling puts are still bid on the risk reversal. I think most people are still buying puts for protection," the trader added. "I think people are still leery of this first budget (July 2) by the new (U.K.) administration...even though obviously sterling looks great."
The sterling puts were also slightly bid in the sterling/mark cross at roughly 0.0/0.2 points, he said.
But dollar/mark one-month vol had moved comparatively little and stood barely changed at 8.35/8.55 versus Tuesday.
